**Rivers that wind like rivers.** The course of a river from the River tool could loop back on itself near its source, where its water had wandered round a shallow hollow before spilling out, and ran in straight lines and stairs along the map's grid where its way had been found from cell to cell. Its loops are now cut straight across (never over higher ground), its runs along the grid are smoothed, and on gentle ground it meanders gently, about half its width to either side over some ten times its width, without climbing out of its valley; the points you drag it through stay where they are, and the course shown before digging is the one dug. On "Continent and islands", a river that took 946 blocks to reach the sea, a hook of 400 blocks round a hollow near its source, now gets there in 483.
